summary: CCC steel tower raised in 1937 in eleven days, deep in the NJ Pine Barrens, still clearing its own sightlines as of 2018.

facts.design: 80-foot steel tower, 7'x7' metal cab, McClintock-Marshall style with an Aermotor Co. nameplate

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps, reportedly in 11 days
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register as US 243, NJ 5, December 15, 1997
NJ Forest Fire Service sought Pinelands Commission approval to clear ~16 acres of pine obstructing the tower's view

evidence.quote: It was constructed by the CCC in 1937, reportedly in just 11 days.

evidence.supports: 80 ft steel tower, 7x7 cab, McClintock-Marshall, Aermotor nameplate
evidence.quote: The 80 steel tower with 7’ x 7’ metal cab is a McClintock-Marshall style but has an Aermotor Co. nameplate.

evidence.supports: in active service (as of register listing)
US 243 / NJ 5 register numbers, location in Bass River State Forest, Burlington County
evidence.quote: Bass River Fire Tower US 243, NJ 5

evidence.supports: 2018 plan to clear 16 acres of pine obstructing the tower's view
evidence.quote: A plan to clearcut 16 acres of White Pine and Loblolly Pine trees, which are obstructing the view from an 80-foot tall fire lookout tower in Bass River Township, and replace them with short growing trees, is poised for passage next week by the Pinelands Commission.

evidence.supports: mayor Deborah Buzby-Cope on the commission's recommendation
evidence.quote: Bass River Mayor Deborah Buzby-Cope said on Monday that the township received notification that the commission's executive director, Nancy Wittenberg, is recommending the commission approve the plan during its scheduled July 13 meeting.

sources.title: List of New Jersey Forest Fire Service fire towers

notes_for_editor: Current public access, climbability, and staffing status (volunteer vs. paid, active vs. seasonal) were not confirmed in this pass; the NJ DEP detection-program page would not render via the text fetcher (JS-only or blocked). The elevation_m (14.3) and height_m (24.0) already in the tower record match the Wikipedia fire-tower table's 47 ft elevation / 80 ft height for this tower, so no correction is needed there.
